record.paper_title: The True Prosoluble Completion of a Group: Examples and Open Problems
record.original_question: For an abstract group Gamma that is not residually soluble, what can be said about the true prosoluble kernel Ker(Gamma -> PS(Gamma))? Equivalently, determine the intersection over n >= 0 of D_n(Gamma), where D_0(Gamma)=Gamma and D_{n+1}(Gamma)=[D_n(Gamma),D_n(Gamma)] is the ordinary derived series. In particular, investigate this kernel for non-residually-soluble one-relator groups, wreath products as in the paper, free products of nilpotent groups with amalgamation, parafree groups, and meta-residually soluble groups, including free-by-free groups that are not residually soluble.

properties of the true prosoluble kernel

Examples to investigate include: other one–relator groups which are not residually soluble; wreath products as in (6.B); free products of nilpotent groups with amalgamation (see for example Proposition 7 in [Kahro1]); parafree groups (see (7.B)); meta–residually soluble groups, namely groups having a residually soluble normal subgroup with residually soluble quotient (see Theorem 2 in [Kahro2]); particular cases: free–by–free groups which are not residually soluble.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Gamma$ be an abstract (discrete) group. Define the ordinary derived series of $\Gamma$ by $D_0(\Gamma) = \Gamma$ and $D_{n+1}(\Gamma) = [D_n(\Gamma), D_n(\Gamma)]$ for $n \geq 0$. The group $\Gamma$ is called residually soluble if $\bigcap_{n \geq 0} D_n(\Gamma) = \{1\}$. The true prosoluble completion $PS(\Gamma)$ is the inverse limit of the system of all finite-index-or-not soluble quotients of $\Gamma$ (equivalently, the inverse limit of $\Gamma/D_n(\Gamma)$ over $n \geq 0$ together with further soluble refinements), and the kernel of the natural map $\Gamma \to PS(\Gamma)$ — called the true prosoluble kernel of $\Gamma$ — coincides with
$$K(\Gamma) := \bigcap_{n=0}^{\infty} D_n(\Gamma).$$

Investigate the structure of $K(\Gamma)$ for groups $\Gamma$ that are not residually soluble. In particular:

(i) Determine $K(\Gamma)$ for non-residually-soluble one-relator groups.

(ii) Determine $K(\Gamma)$ for wreath products $A \wr B$ of suitable groups $A, B$ that fail to be residually soluble.

(iii) Determine $K(\Gamma)$ for free products with amalgamation $N_1 *_H N_2$ where $N_1, N_2$ are nilpotent groups.

(iv) Determine $K(\Gamma)$ for parafree groups $\Gamma$ (i.e., residually nilpotent groups having the same nilpotent quotients as some free group) which are not residually soluble.

(v) Determine $K(\Gamma)$ for meta-residually-soluble groups, i.e., groups $\Gamma$ admitting a normal subgroup $N \trianglelefteq \Gamma$ such that both $N$ and $\Gamma/N$ are residually soluble; in particular for free-by-free groups that are not residually soluble.

Give meaningful descriptions, examples, or structural theorems describing $K(\Gamma)$ in each of these classes.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as a general open research direction concerning the true prosoluble kernel of non-residually-soluble groups. No comprehensive solution covering the listed classes (non-residually-soluble one-relator groups, certain wreath products, amalgams of nilpotent groups, parafree groups, meta-residually-soluble and free-by-free groups) appears to be known; the question remains an open program with only partial examples available.
